title: Burning rubber smell
h1: Why does my car smell like burning rubber?
metaDesc: Burning rubber or hot brake smell? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's the brakes, a belt, the clutch or something touching the exhaust, and how urgent it is.
synonyms: burning smell from under the car
intro: A burning rubber smell usually comes from something rubbing, slipping or getting too hot: brakes, a drive belt, the clutch, or a hose or bit of debris touching the hot exhaust. Where the smell comes from and when you notice it narrows it down fast. Answer the questions below to see the likely cause and how soon to act.
safety: If you see smoke from a wheel or from under the hood, pull over, turn off the engine and step away from the car.
If the brake pedal feels soft, sinks or the car won't stop normally, pull over as soon as it's safe and don't drive on.
Don't touch the wheels, brakes or exhaust after a burning smell. They can be hot enough to burn you.

q_smoke.q: Do you see smoke, or does anything else feel wrong along with the smell?
q_smoke.help: Look at each wheel and at the hood. Smoke near one wheel almost always means a brake problem.

opts.a: Smoke from one wheel, or one wheel is much hotter than the others
The brake pedal feels soft or different, or the red brake light is on

q_when.q: When do you notice the smell?

opts.a: After a long downhill, heavy braking, or pulling a trailer
After driving with the parking brake partly on
From under the hood, often with a squeal on startup or when the A/C kicks on
When pulling away or going uphill in a manual car
During normal driving, with no obvious reason

q_drive_feel.q: Does the car feel or sound different while you drive?
q_drive_feel.help: A brake that won't fully let go makes the car feel like it's being held back, as if you're driving with the brakes lightly on.

opts.a: It feels held back, pulls to one side, or coasts poorly
A rubbing or scraping sound, especially when turning or over bumps
It drives normally, the smell just comes and goes
It smells more like burning plastic than rubber

result.title: A brake may be stuck on and overheating, or the brake system may have a problem
result.now: Pull over somewhere safe, turn off the engine and let the brakes cool. Don't drive it further. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If there are flames or the smoke gets heavier, get everyone away from the car and call 911.

If the parking brake was on, release it fully and let everything cool for at least 30 minutes. Even if the smell clears, overheated brakes can be weakened, so have them checked before driving further.
If the brake pedal feels soft, sinks, or the red brake warning light is on, the brakes may not stop the car normally. Don't drive it, even after it cools.
result.why: When a brake doesn't release, it rubs constantly and builds up a lot of heat. That heat can boil the brake fluid and burn the pads, which can leave you with weak or failing brakes. A soft pedal or red brake light can also mean the hydraulic system is losing pressure. In rare cases an overheated brake can start a fire.

causes.name: Stuck brake caliper
causes.clues: Smoke or smell from one wheel, the car pulls to one side, or that wheel is far hotter than the others.
causes.against: If all four wheels feel about the same, a single stuck caliper is less likely.

causes.name: Parking brake not fully released or sticking
causes.clues: It's coming from a rear wheel, or the parking brake light stayed on.

causes.name: Collapsed brake hose holding pressure on one wheel
causes.clues: The problem started or got worse after heavy braking.
causes.against: Less common than a stuck caliper.

causes.name: Low brake fluid or a hydraulic problem
causes.clues: The pedal feels soft or sinks, or the red brake light stays on with the parking brake released.

you: Without touching anything, look for smoke near each wheel.
Check that the parking brake is fully released.
Once everything is cool, check the brake fluid level in the reservoir.
shop: Brake inspection with the wheels off
Brake hose and fluid condition check
Wheel temperature comparison after a short test

result.title: Something under the hood is burning or slipping badly
result.now: Pull over, turn off the engine and step away from the car. Don't open the hood if you see flames. Once it has cooled and there's no fire, have it towed.
if: If you see flames, get everyone away from the car and call 911.
If the smoke stops once the engine is off and you can see a shredded or missing belt, it still needs a tow. The belt often drives the water pump and the charging system.
If the temperature gauge was climbing or a red warning light came on, don't restart the engine.
result.why: Smoke from under the hood with a rubber smell usually means a belt is slipping or shredding, a hose is melting against something hot, or fluid is burning on the engine. Any of these can lead to overheating, a dead battery or a fire if you keep driving.

causes.name: Slipping or failing drive belt
causes.clues: A loud squeal, a battery or temperature warning, or heavy steering.

causes.name: Seized pulley, A/C compressor or other belt-driven part
causes.clues: A grinding or squealing noise that started recently.

causes.name: Hose or wiring touching a hot part
causes.clues: A smell that's more like melting plastic, or a hose that's been recently worked on.

causes.name: Oil or fluid leaking onto the hot exhaust
causes.clues: A recent oil change or a known leak, and blue-gray smoke.

shop: Drive belt, tensioner and pulley inspection
Check of belt-driven parts for a seized bearing

result.title: The brakes may have gotten very hot from heavy use
result.now: If you can, pull over safely and let the brakes cool for 20–30 minutes. On long downhills, use a lower gear so the engine helps slow the car and you don't ride the brakes.
if: If the pedal felt soft, sank, or the car took longer to stop, don't drive on after it cools. Have the brakes and brake fluid checked first. Overheated fluid can leave the brakes weak.
If the smell keeps coming back during normal driving, a brake may be dragging. Get it checked within a few days.
If you see smoke from a wheel, one wheel stays much hotter than the others, or the car pulls to one side, don't drive further until the brakes are checked.
result.why: Long downhill stretches and heavy loads make the brakes work hard. The pads can get hot enough to give off a sharp, burnt smell. A one-time smell after that kind of driving is common, but very hot brakes don't stop as well until they cool.

causes.name: Brakes overheated from heavy use
causes.clues: It happened on a steep descent, in mountain driving, or while hauling.
causes.against: If the smell shows up on flat roads with light braking, look for a dragging brake instead.

causes.name: New brake pads bedding in
causes.clues: The pads were replaced recently.

causes.name: Dragging brake made worse by heavy use
causes.clues: One wheel stays much hotter, or the smell lingers after it cools.

you: After it cools, see if the car rolls freely and doesn't pull to one side.
Notice whether the smell returns during normal, gentle driving.
shop: Brake fluid condition and moisture test

result.title: The parking brake may have been rubbing while you drove
result.now: Release the parking brake fully, check that its warning light goes out, and let the wheels cool before driving on.
if: If the smell continues once it's fully released, the parking brake may be sticking. Have it checked within a few days.
If you drove a long way with it on, have the rear brakes inspected. The pads or shoes may be glazed or worn.
If the pedal feels soft or different, the car takes longer to stop, or the red brake light stays on after release, don't drive it until the brakes are checked.
If you see smoke from a wheel, keep clear and let it cool.
result.why: Driving with the parking brake partly on makes the rear brakes rub the whole time. That creates heat and a strong burnt smell. Once it's released and cooled, the smell usually fades. If it doesn't, something may still be dragging.

causes.name: Parking brake not fully released
causes.clues: The parking brake light was on, or you forgot to release it.

causes.name: Sticking parking brake cable or mechanism
causes.clues: It was released, but a rear wheel still drags. This is more common in winter or on older cars.

you: Make sure the parking brake lever, pedal or button is fully off.
After cooling, push the car gently on a flat surface to see if it rolls freely.
shop: Parking brake cable and adjustment check
Electronic parking brake scan if equipped

result.title: A drive belt may be slipping
result.now: Have the belt, tensioner and pulleys checked within the next few days. Keep trips short until then.
if: If the battery light or temperature warning comes on, or steering gets heavy, pull over and stop. The belt may have broken. Have it towed.
If you see smoke from under the hood, turn off the engine and don't drive it.
result.why: The drive belt runs the alternator, and on many cars the water pump and power steering. When it slips over a pulley, the friction makes a burnt rubber smell and often a squeal. A slipping belt can wear through and snap. A shop will usually check the tensioner and pulleys before replacing the belt, since a bad pulley will ruin a new belt.

causes.name: Worn or glazed drive belt
causes.clues: Cracks or a shiny surface on the belt, and a squeal on cold starts.

causes.name: Weak belt tensioner
causes.clues: The tensioner arm bounces or the belt flaps at idle.

causes.name: Pulley or belt-driven part starting to seize
causes.clues: The smell is worse with the A/C on, or there's a grinding or whirring noise.

causes.name: Fluid on the belt
causes.clues: A leak of oil, coolant or power steering fluid near the front of the engine.

you: With the engine off, look at the belt for cracks, fraying or a shiny glazed surface.
Notice whether the smell or squeal gets worse with the A/C on.
shop: Check of belt-driven parts for bearing noise

result.title: The clutch is likely slipping or being overworked
result.now: Have the clutch checked within a few days. Until then, pull away gently and avoid resting your foot on the clutch pedal.
if: If the engine revs rise but the car doesn't speed up to match, the clutch is slipping. Get it checked as soon as you can.
If you see smoke from under the car or it won't move in gear, stop and have it towed.
result.why: A clutch that slips turns engine power into heat instead of motion, which gives off a sharp burnt smell. A single smell after a tricky hill start is common. A smell that keeps coming back often means the clutch is worn.

causes.name: Worn clutch
causes.clues: The engine revs climb in high gears without the car speeding up, especially uphill.

causes.name: Driving habit (riding the clutch or slow hill starts)
causes.clues: It only happens after hill starts, heavy loads or stop-and-go traffic.

causes.name: Oil contaminating the clutch
causes.clues: A known engine or transmission oil leak, and grabbing or slipping.

you: On a quiet, safe road, in a high gear at a low speed, press the gas firmly once. If the revs jump without the car speeding up, the clutch is slipping. Don't repeat it, since each try adds heat.
Notice whether the clutch now engages higher in the pedal travel than it used to.
shop: Inspection for oil leaks at the bellhousing

result.title: A brake may be dragging
result.now: Pull over somewhere safe, turn off the engine and let the brakes cool. Don't drive further until the brakes are checked. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If you see smoke from a wheel, keep everyone clear and let it cool. Call 911 if you see flames.
If the brake pedal feels soft, sinks, or the red brake light comes on, the brakes may not stop the car normally. Don't move it.
If the parking brake was partly on, release it fully and let everything cool. Overheated brakes can still be weakened, so have them checked before relying on the car.
result.why: When a brake doesn't fully let go, it rubs constantly. That makes the car feel held back, can pull it to one side, and creates a hot, burnt smell. A brake hot enough to smell can fade and stop the car less well, and it can overheat further if you keep driving.

causes.name: Sticking caliper or caliper slides
causes.clues: The car pulls to one side, and one wheel is hotter or has more brake dust.

causes.name: Sticking parking brake
causes.clues: The drag seems to come from the rear.

causes.name: Worn brake hose or brake fluid problem
causes.clues: More than one wheel drags, or the pedal feels different.

you: After it has cooled, carefully hold your hand near (not on) each wheel to compare heat. Don't drive just to test it.
Look for one wheel with much more brake dust than the others.
shop: Brake inspection with the wheels off

result.title: Something may be rubbing on a tire or touching the hot exhaust
result.now: When the car has cooled, look under it and around the tires for a plastic bag, loose shield, sagging hose or rubbed tire. Book a check if you can't find the source.
if: If a tire shows a bald strip, bulge or rubbed sidewall, have it looked at before your next drive.
If the smell gets stronger or you see smoke, pull over and turn off the engine.
If the car starts pulling to one side or feels held back, a brake may be dragging. Pull over, let it cool, and have it checked before driving further.
result.why: A smell that comes and goes, without any change in how the car drives, often comes from something brushing a tire when you turn, or a bit of plastic or rubber stuck on the hot exhaust. These are usually easy to fix once found.

causes.name: Debris stuck on the exhaust
causes.clues: You recently drove over trash or a plastic bag, and the smell is strongest after you stop.

causes.name: Tire rubbing on the fender liner or a part
causes.clues: A rubbing sound when turning or over bumps, new or larger tires, or a loose plastic liner.

causes.name: Hose or wire resting on a hot part
causes.clues: The smell comes from under the hood, and a hose or clip looks out of place.

causes.name: Small oil leak dripping onto the exhaust
causes.clues: Oily spots under the engine, or a smell more like hot oil.

you: Once everything is cool, look under the car and along the exhaust for anything stuck to it.
Turn the steering fully each way and look for rub marks on the tires and liners.

result.title: A burning plastic smell can be wiring, or plastic touching something hot
result.now: Don't drive it until you know where the smell is coming from. Park, turn off the engine, and once it's cool, look under the car for plastic stuck to the exhaust. If you can't find an outside source, or the smell comes from the dash, vents or under the hood, have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If you see smoke from the dash, vents or under the hood, pull over, turn off the engine and get out.
If a fuse keeps blowing or something electrical stops working along with the smell, don't drive it until it's checked.
If you find only a melted bag or bit of plastic on the exhaust, have it removed once everything is cool. If the smell keeps coming back after that, have the car checked.
result.why: A burning plastic smell can come from something minor, like a bag melting on the exhaust. It can also come from overheated wiring, a failing blower motor or a short circuit, which can lead to a fire. From the driver's seat there's no reliable way to tell which, so it's worth finding the source before driving on.

causes.name: Plastic stuck to the exhaust
causes.clues: The smell is strongest outside the car, near the back or underneath.

causes.name: Overheating electrical part or wiring
causes.clues: The smell comes through the vents or dash, or something electrical acts up.

causes.name: Failing heater blower motor or resistor
causes.clues: The smell starts when the fan is on, or some fan speeds don't work.

you: Notice whether the smell changes when you turn the fan, heater or A/C on and off.
Once cool, look under the car for melted plastic on the exhaust.
shop: Electrical system inspection for heat damage

result.title: Have the brakes and belts checked to find the source
result.now: Note when the smell shows up and where it seems strongest, then have the brakes and under-hood area inspected within a few days.
if: If you see smoke, the brake pedal changes, or a warning light comes on, pull over and stop.
If the smell gets stronger with each drive, get it checked within a day or two.
If one wheel is much hotter than the others or the car pulls to one side, a brake may be dragging. Don't drive further until it's checked.
result.why: Most burning rubber smells come from the brakes, a belt, the clutch or something touching the exhaust. A technician can usually narrow down the source with a careful look and a short test drive.

causes.name: Dragging brake
causes.clues: The smell is near a wheel, or the car feels held back.

causes.name: Slipping drive belt
causes.clues: The smell is under the hood, with a squeal.

causes.name: Something touching the exhaust
causes.clues: The smell is strongest after you park.

you: Write down when you notice the smell and whether it's stronger near one wheel or the hood.
